registeredPageErrata.reason: p0140#8 defines D on SC and SD = SN; fig160 identifies alpha as angle CSB = angle DSB. Cosine law in the stated triangles BSD and BSN gives DB^2 = SB^2 + SD^2 - 2 SB SD cos(alpha) and NB^2 = SB^2 + SN^2 - 2 SB SN cos(angle NSB). Since SD = SN > 0 and p0141#1 gives DB > NB, subtraction forces cos(alpha) < cos(angle NSB), not cos(angle NSD). On [0, pi], cosine is strictly decreasing, so the already printed conclusion angle NSB < alpha follows. No incidence identifies angle NSD with angle NSB; an exact nondegenerate example satisfying gamma maximal makes the printed NSD inequality false. This is a source-bound mathematical printing-error proposal, not a typography guess or a source-transcription change.
